subject: Asterion: Sentry on‑prem K8s launch playbook and IO commitments
body:
From: Ethan Moore <ethan@asterion.ai>
To: karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Cc: priya@asterion.ai
Date: Mon, 01 Jul 2028 15:08:00 -0700
Subject: Kickoff: on‑prem 'Sentry' cluster for Asterion (high-IO)

Hi Karthik —

Thanks for the intro call last week. We want to move forward with a private (on‑prem VPC) deployment for our Sentry inference cluster. Key constraints:
- Dataset access is local (NVMe-backed) with bursty training/inference patterns.
- Required 99th percentile tail latency target: 120ms for 4k token sequences.
- Multi-tenant: three product teams (real‑time inference, batch embedding jobs, evals).
- Compliance: box‑level encryption + integration with our Vault KMS.

Can you share a proposed node / storage architecture and a short launch playbook so we can align procurement and facility lead? Attaching our baseline perf traces and a short network diagram.

—Ethan
CTO, Asterion AI

From: karthik_iyer@redwood.com <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Ethan Moore <ethan@asterion.ai>
Cc: priya@asterion.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.com, neha_kapoor@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 02 Jul 2028 10:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Kickoff: on‑prem 'Sentry' cluster for Asterion (high-IO)

Ethan / Priya —

Thanks — excited to get this moving. High level we recommend a 3‑phase launch playbook (discovery -> sprint zero -> production handoff). To speed things up I sketched an initial node/storage topology and a kickoff agenda (see attached 'asterion-sprint-plan.xlsx'). Quick ask before we schedule a deep technical workshop:
1) Do you have a preferred CSI driver (Ceph/Rook vs vendor iSCSI)?
2) Are customer ops able to place NVMe as local ephemeral for low-latency KV caching?
3) Who will own KMS/Vault integration on your side (name + contact)?

I'll let Marissa/Neha lead the technical specifics below. Proposed times for workshop: Thu 07/05 9–11am PT or Mon 07/09 10–12pm PT.

Cheers,
Karthik
Solutions Director, Redwood Inference

From: marissa_cole@redwood.com <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Ethan Moore <ethan@asterion.ai>, karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Cc: neha_kapoor@redwood.com, priya@asterion.ai
Date: Thu, 05 Jul 2028 08:14:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Kickoff: on‑prem 'Sentry' cluster for Asterion (high-IO)

Ethan / Priya —

Thanks for the perf traces. Below is a concise operational proposal (node classes, PV choices, networking gates, and a short sprint checklist). This is deliberately prescriptive to reduce back-and-forth during procurement.

1) Cluster footprint and node roles (initial pilot: 3 racks)
- control-plane: 3x m5c-xx (or equivalent vm/flavor) — dedicated masters (HA)
- infra/ops: 2x c5d-2xlarge for logging, monitoring, and CSI controllers
- compute-shared: 6x g1-48g (GPUs for mixed small/medium models) — 1TB NVMe local for transient caches
- compute-gpu-heavy: 4x g2-80g (GPU heavy instances) with 2 x 1.6TB NVMe per node (for model shards + KV cache)
- io-edge: 3x i3en-style servers (24 NVMe) mapped to blockstore tier for hot datasets (exported via iSCSI/CSI)
Notes: node sizes are vendor-neutral references — procurement can map to the customer's preferred OEM. The 'io-edge' nodes run the persistent local blockstore (see PVs below) and present volumes via CSI to the cluster.

2) Storage topology and PV classes
- local-ephemeral-nvme: StorageClass (ephemeral) — hostPath / local PV for prefix/KV caching (no replication, fast attach). Mount options: noatime, nodelalloc. 
- blockstore-hdd: StorageClass backed by ceph-block (replicated RBD) — for model artifacts and long‑term volumes. Replication: 3x, encrypted at rest via customer KMS.
- hot-block-iscsi: StorageClass exported from iSCSI gateway on io-edge nodes — intended for dataset slices requiring very high IOPS and locality. Use multipath, discard enabled.
- logs-nfs: StorageClass (NFSv4) — for centralized logs/diagnostics, backed by a small HA NAS cluster.

3) IO guarantees and eviction policy
- Configure kubelet eviction thresholds: memory.available 200Mi, nodefs.available 10%, imagefs.available 15%.
- Use CRD-based pod classes: realtime-inference (low latency, high priority), batch (lower priority, scheduled on cheaper compute).
- For the realtime-inference class set resourceRequests to reserve 30% CPU and 25% GPU headroom to prevent noisy neighbor issues.

4) Networking and routing
- VPC peering to customer's ops VLAN with BGP; egress through a pair of NAT gateways in each rack.
- Enforce MTU 9000 on inter-node links and jumbo frames across NVMe-over-Fabric paths.
- Traffic shaping: kube-proxy in IPVS mode; CNI: Calico with eBPF data plane for host-level policy enforcement.

5) Security and compliance
- All block volumes encrypted with customer Vault KMS (we will provide sample KMS mapping).
- Audit logging: enable API server audit policy with 90-day retention (forwarded to a secured SIEM).
- Pod Security Standards: enforce restricted profiles for production namespaces.

6) Sprint zero checklist (2 weeks)
- Rack inventory and power budget verified by customer ops. Owner: Priya
- NVMe mounting test and latency validation (fio profile attached): Owner: Asterion infra
- CSI integration smoke test (create/delete, snapshot, restore): Owner: Marissa/Redwood
- KMS key rotation handshake and test restores: Owner: Neha/Redwood + Priya
- Canary rollout for realtime-inference route (start 5% traffic -> 25% -> 100%): Owner: Karthik

7) Quick numbers (pilot):
- Onboarding compute: ~13 nodes (estimate)
- Blockstore usable capacity (replicated): 200 TB (depends on RAID/ceph profile)
- Expected baseline 95th token cost improvement from prefix caching: 30–40%

Next steps: confirm procurement window (target Q3 rack build) and pick workshop slot. I recommend Thu 07/05 9–11am PT (we can use this to lock architecture and record a short acceptance test matrix).

Action items:
- Priya: confirm NVMe policy (can you allow local NVMe on compute nodes?)
- Ethan: share contact for KMS owner (we need a technical contact)
- Priya + Asterion infra: run fio profile in attachment and drop results to the Drive link

Cheers,
Marissa Cole
Head of Solutions Engineering, Redwood Inference

Attachment references: 'pv-sizing.csv' (simple PV capacity model), 'sentry-network-drawing.png' (diagram), 'asterion-sprint-plan.xlsx'

From: Priya Deshmukh <priya@asterion.ai>
To: marissa_cole@redwood.com, karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Cc: neha_kapoor@redwood.com, Ethan Moore <ethan@asterion.ai>
Date: Mon, 15 Jul 2028 09:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Kickoff: on‑prem 'Sentry' cluster for Asterion (high-IO)

Marissa / Karthik —

Thanks for the clear plan and checklist. Quick responses:
- NVMe local on compute nodes: approved for pilot (we will allocate local 1TB per compute‑shared node and 2x1.6TB on gpu‑heavy nodes).
- CSI: we prefer to start with Ceph RBD (we have an existing Ceph ops team), but we will stand up an iSCSI gateway on the io-edge hosts for the hottest datasets.
- KMS owner: Rahul Patel (rahul.p@asterion.ai) — Rahul will take the KMS workstream and coordinate with Neha.

Workshop: Mon 07/09 10–12pm PT works best for the ops team (Priya, Rahul, Ethan). Please send an invite and share the Drive link with the acceptance test spreadsheet.

We attached initial fio results on the drive; baseline looks within expected variance. We'll prepare rack power numbers and an initial BOM by Friday.

Regards,
Priya Deshmukh
Head of Platform Engineering, Asterion AI
